problem_statement: The Jeyla Danishyan-Abuzar Music Blog Website Template, already rebranded as 'Tidepool Frequencies' (a coastal field-recording and ambient music journal by recordist Marisol Vantar), is a directly runnable single-file static blog (index.html, style.css, local images/*.jpg, no build step) with a fixed masthead, a hero, a Featured Listening Queue of three recording cards (Slack Tide / Salt Cedar / Foghorn Drone), long-form field-note articles, a sidebar of widgets, and a footer. Grow the Featured Listening Queue into a small design-system component: (1) add an on-page listening-queue filter above the three recording cards with topic chips (All recordings / Hydrophone / Tape Loops / Drone) and a live 'Now cued' status readout, wired end to end so clicking a chip filters the cards AND updates the status to reflect the selection (e.g. clicking Tape Loops sets 'Now cued 1 recording: Salt Cedar.'); and (2) add a shared 'Listening queue rail' component that appears consistently in THREE sections of the page — inside the Featured Listening Queue, in the sidebar (#side-section), and in the footer (#end) — so a reader in any part of the journal can jump back to a recording source. The filter strip and the rail must keep the existing black/red editorial visual language and must be responsive so the page has NO horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile viewport. Preserve the Tidepool masthead, hero, the three recording cards and local images, the article field notes, the sidebar widgets, and the footer.
required_content: Keep the rebranded Tidepool Frequencies masthead, hero, and the Featured Listening Queue heading with the three recordings Slack Tide (hydrophone / estuary), Salt Cedar (tape loops), and Foghorn Drone (Heceta Head).

Add an on-page listening-queue filter above the three recording cards: an eyebrow, the heading 'Filter the Featured Listening Queue', four topic chips (All recordings / Hydrophone / Tape Loops / Drone), and a live '.queue-status' 'Now cued' readout.

Add a shared 'Listening queue rail' component (eyebrow 'LISTENING QUEUE RAIL' + source links) consistently in THREE sections — inside the Featured Listening Queue (.queue-rail--featured), in the sidebar (.queue-rail--sidebar), and in the footer (.queue-rail--footer) — so the same component appears in each region, not only in one.

Style the filter strip and the shared rail to match the reference black/red editorial look (black panels, red accents) — the rendered filter panel must be visually faithful to the reference, not a collapsed or off-palette restyle.

Make the filter strip responsive so the page has NO horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile viewport (let the chips wrap / use a fluid layout instead of a fixed-width non-wrapping row); do not merely clip the overflow with overflow-x:hidden — the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width. Keep desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) free of horizontal overflow.

Keep the listening-queue filter fully wired end to end: clicking a topic chip (Tape Loops / Hydrophone / All recordings) must update the '.queue-status' readout to reflect the selection (e.g. clicking Tape Loops yields 'Now cued 1 recording: Salt Cedar.'), in addition to highlighting the active chip and hiding non-matching cards — the post-click terminal state must reflect the selected topic, not the default 'Now cued 3 recordings'.
Do not damage the existing Tidepool masthead, hero, the three recording cards, the long-form field-note articles, the sidebar widgets, the local images, or the footer; keep the branding.
design_constraints: Keep the black/red/white Tidepool editorial visual language, strong display titles, and the compact card / article / sidebar rhythm; the filter panel and rail must look native to the page, not a bolted-on benchmark panel.
Do not replace the blog, the Featured Listening Queue, or the page with a new app shell, framework, external design system, or unrelated layout.
Do not remove the filter panel, the four topic chips, the shared rail, the recording cards, the hero, the navigation, or the filter script.

Do not add npm dependencies, remote scripts, remote fonts, remote images, generated build outputs, or unrelated file churn; keep the single-file static architecture (index.html, style.css, and the queue-filter.js interaction script).
The filter strip and rail must fit within 1440px desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile viewports without horizontal overflow, and render in the Tidepool black/red palette.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial capture the rebranded Tidepool masthead, title and hero above the fold.

desktop_featured_component and mobile_featured_component scroll to the listening-queue filter panel and verify the 'Filter the Featured Listening Queue' heading, the chips, and the status readout render in the black/red palette on desktop and 390px mobile (the visual-fidelity states).

desktop_tape_filter / desktop_hydrophone_filter / desktop_all_reset / mobile_tape_filter click the topic chips and verify the '.queue-status' readout updates to reflect the selection (the interaction-trajectory states); their before-state is desktop_featured_component.

desktop_side_posts_regression scrolls to #side-section and desktop_footer_regression scrolls to #end; both verify the shared 'Listening queue rail' (.queue-rail--sidebar / .queue-rail--footer) is present, proving the component appears consistently across sections.

desktop_featured_listening_queue / mobile_featured_listening_queue, desktop_blog_cards_regression, desktop_article_regression and desktop_inspiration_regression check the recordings, cards, field notes, and local imagery survive.

Baseline captures still complete (the page structure is intact); a fixed-width non-wrapping chip row, a rail present only in the featured section, a collapsed off-palette strip, or a filter that does not re-sync its status readout are scored as overflow / cross-section / visual / interaction failures, not capture failures.

change_completion: The listening-queue filter (four topic chips + status readout) sits above the three recording cards on the page.
The shared 'Listening queue rail' appears in the featured, sidebar, and footer sections.
On mobile the page has no horizontal overflow after the responsive layout.
content_asset_continuity: The recordings stay grounded in the repo's local card images (blog.img / blog-2.img / blog-3.img); no external or placeholder media.
The Tidepool masthead, hero, cards, articles, and sidebar are preserved.
design_consistency: The filter strip and shared rail keep the black/red editorial style and are visually faithful to the reference.
The same listening-queue rail is consistent across the featured / sidebar / footer sections; the hero, cards, and masthead remain recognizable.
interaction_continuity: Clicking a topic chip updates the 'Now cued' status readout to the selection (the post-click terminal state reflects the change, not the default).
The All-recordings reset restores the full three-recording view and status.
regression: The Tidepool masthead, hero, cards, field notes, sidebar, and footer retain their branding and imagery.
No package, build system, backend, remote asset, generated build artifact, or broad redesign is introduced. Hidden text, fake asset references, or a simplified mock must not pass.
responsive: The page has no horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile states.
Desktop and tablet states remain free of horizontal overflow.

scoring_notes: A correct patch is a full-page editorial restyle/rebrand that turns the generic Ludovico music-blog demo into the Tidepool Frequencies coastal field-recording journal: a rebranded masthead and hero, a visible Featured Listening Queue built from the existing three cards and local images, rewritten long-form field notes, rebranded sidebar widgets and footer, and no leftover Ludovico / Lorem-ipsum / fashion demo copy, all within the single-file static HTML/CSS architecture and running clean (no console or network errors, no horizontal overflow). A masthead-only shallow rebrand that leaves the queue, articles, sidebar or footer as the demo, or the untouched original demo, must not pass.

metadata.design_goal: use real repo content, media, icons, copy, and data structures without generic dummy surfaces
metadata.selected_repo_reason: The Music Blog Website Template is a runnable static HTML/CSS editorial blog with real local music-card images, a multi-section layout (hero, blog cards, long-form articles, sidebar widgets, footer) and no build step, making it a natural full-page content/asset-continuity restyle/rebrand task.
